title: Bracing for Impact — How the 2026 El Niño Affects Brazil's Agriculture
summary: NOAA expects El Niño to reach very strong intensity in Nov 2026–Jan 2027, during Brazil's planting and vegetative phases. North, Northeast and north-west Centre-West face heat and below-average rain; the South faces excess rain and floods; the Southeast is the least affected but faces irregular rain and heatwaves (risk rated medium-high).

impact.coffee: Southeast coffee needs a dry spell followed by steady rain for flowering. El Niño years bring irregular rain that disrupts flowering, fruit set, filling and bean weight; heat can cause uneven flowering and flower abortion. Post expects a negative production impact that grows with how irregular rain is at critical stages.
impact.sugar: Irregular winter rain in the Centre-South can interrupt harvesting and slow crushing; excess moisture delays sugar concentration (lower ATR and quality). Summer dryness and heat, mainly in the North/Northeast, can hurt planting, development and yields.
impact.cotton: Heat and low soil moisture can cut yields. Second-crop cotton follows soybeans, so late soybean planting from irregular rain shortens the cotton window; Post sees the impact as possibly limited, since 2025/26 still produced a large crop despite late planting.
